title: Simple-root reflections generate the root reflection group
statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real vector space [def-weil-vector-space-dimension] with a positive definite symmetric bilinear form $(\ ,\ )$. For $a\ne0$ write $s_a(x)=x-2(x,a)(a,a)^{-1}a$. Let $R\subset V\setminus\{0\}$ be finite and span $V$, with $R\cap\mathbf R a=\{a,-a\}$ for every $a\in R$, each $s_a$ permuting $R$, and $2(b,a)(a,a)^{-1}\in\mathbf Z$ for $a,b\in R$. Let $D\subseteq R$ be a real basis of $V$ such that each root has integer $D$-coordinates all nonnegative or all nonpositive. Then every $s_b$ for $b\in R$ is a finite product of the $s_a$ for $a\in D$. Consequently the subgroup of $\operatorname{GL}_{\mathbf R}(V)$ generated by all root reflections equals the subgroup generated by the simple-root reflections. Empty products and the empty root system are included.

source.place: Appendix C.11, printed p.610, first assertion only; C.21--C.22, printed p.612. Height-descent argument underlying simple-reflection generation.

proof.text: Substitution into the reflection formula gives $s_{-a}=s_a$, $s_a(a)=-a$ and $s_a^2=1$. Thus $-R=R$. Bilinearity gives $(s_ax,s_ay)=(x,y)$: on writing $A=(a,a)$, the two cross terms sum to $-4(x,a)(y,a)/A$ and the quadratic term is $4(x,a)(y,a)/A$. In particular the reflections are invertible linear maps. If $R=\varnothing$, spanning forces $V=0$, $D=\varnothing$, and both generated subgroups consist of the identity (the empty product). Henceforth assume $R\ne\varnothing$.

e a$ is positive: otherwise $b\in R\cap\mathbf R a=\{a,-a\}$, and positivity would give $b=a$.

source.place: Appendix C.11 (first assertion), printed p.610; C.21--C.22, printed p.612. Explicit agent-supplied height-descent proof, step 2

proof.text: Fix a positive root $b\notin D$. Expanding its norm gives $0<(b,b)=\sum_{a\in D}n_a(b,a)$. Therefore some $a\in D$ satisfies $n_a>0$ and $(b,a)>0$. The integer $m=2(b,a)/(a,a)$ is strictly positive. The root $c=s_ab=b-ma$ has the same coordinates as $b$ away from $a$. By the previous step one of those coordinates is positive. Since all coordinates of the root $c$ have the same sign, they must all be nonnegative. Thus $c$ is positive and $1\leq h(c)=h(b)-m<h(b)$. This uses only reducedness, the stated base property, the reflection-permutation hypothesis, and integrality.

source.place: Appendix C.11 (first assertion), printed p.610; C.21--C.22, printed p.612. Explicit agent-supplied height-descent proof, step 3

proof.text: For nonzero $a,b$ put $c=s_ab$. Orthogonality and involutivity from step 1 give $(c,c)=(b,b)$ and $(s_ax,b)=(x,c)$. Linearity then gives, for every $x$, $s_as_bs_a(x)=s_a(s_ax-2(s_ax,b)(b,b)^{-1}b)=x-2(x,c)(c,c)^{-1}c=s_c(x)$. Consequently $s_b=s_as_cs_a$. This is an equality of invertible linear maps, not only of their permutations of $R$.

source.place: Appendix C.11 (first assertion), printed p.610; C.21--C.22, printed p.612. Explicit agent-supplied height-descent proof, step 4

proof.text: Prove by strong induction on $h(b)\in\mathbf Z_{>0}$ that $s_b$ is a finite product of reflections indexed by $D$, for every positive root $b$. If $b\in D$, use the one-letter product. Otherwise step 3 supplies $a\in D$ and a positive root $c=s_ab$ of strictly smaller height. The induction hypothesis writes $s_c$ as such a product; step 4 writes $s_b=s_as_cs_a$, so prepend and append $s_a$. At height $1$, a nonnegative integral coordinate vector of sum $1$ has a single coefficient $1$ and all others $0$, so $b\in D$; thus the induction has a base. For any negative root $b$, apply the positive result to $-b$ and use $s_b=s_{-b}$.

source.place: Appendix C.11 (first assertion), printed p.610; C.21--C.22, printed p.612. Explicit agent-supplied height-descent proof, step 5

proof.text: Every simple-root reflection is a root reflection because $D\subseteq R$, so the subgroup generated by the former is contained in that generated by the latter. Conversely each root reflection belongs to the simple-generated subgroup by step 5. A subgroup containing every generator contains the subgroup they generate, giving the reverse inclusion. The finite products proved above include empty products, whose value is the identity.

lean.statement: theorem simple_root_reflection_generation (V : Type u) [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V] (B : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ V) (hBsymm : B.IsSymm) (hBpos : ∀ x : V, x ≠ 0 → 0 < B x x) (R : Set V) (hRfinite : R.Finite) (hRzero : (0 : V) ∉ R) (hRspan : Submodule.span ℝ R = ⊤) (hRline : ∀ a ∈ R, R ∩ {x : V | ∃ t : ℝ, t • a = x} = {a, -a}) (hRreflect : ∀ a ∈ R, Set.BijOn (fun x : V ↦ x - (2 * B x a * (B a a)⁻¹) • a) R R) (hRint : ∀ a ∈ R, ∀ b ∈ R, ∃ n : ℤ, 2 * B b a * (B a a)⁻¹ = (n : ℝ)) (D : Set V) (hDR : D ⊆ R) (e : Module.Basis D ℝ V) (he : ∀ a : D, e a = (a : V)) (hDcoords : ∀ b ∈ R, ∃ n : D → ℤ, (∀ a : D, (n a : ℝ) = e.repr b a) ∧ ((∀ a : D, 0 ≤ n a) ∨ (∀ a : D, n a ≤ 0))) : (∀ b ∈ R, ∃ w : List (V ≃ₗ[ℝ] V), (∀ g ∈ w, ∃ a ∈ D, ∀ x : V, g x = x - (2 * B x a * (B a a)⁻¹) • a) ∧ (∀ x : V, w.prod x = x - (2 * B x b * (B b b)⁻¹) • b)) ∧ Subgroup.closure {g : V ≃ₗ[ℝ] V | ∃ b ∈ R, ∀ x : V, g x = x - (2 * B x b * (B b b)⁻¹) • b} = Subgroup.closure {g : V ≃ₗ[ℝ] V | ∃ a ∈ D, ∀ x : V, g x = x - (2 * B x a * (B a a)⁻¹) • a}
